China is increasingly relying on Russian oil amid the Iran War.

China’s imports of Russian oil rose by ~200,000 barrels per day in August, to ~1.6 million barrels per day, their highest since March.

This marks the 3rd consecutive monthly increase, bringing the cumulative gain over that stretch to ~500,000 barrels per day.

This is now above the levels seen in the last 4 months of 2025.

By comparison, China imported ~2.0 million barrels per day from Russia in February.

This comes as Middle East oil supplies have become more constrained and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted, prompting Chinese refiners to turn increasingly to Russian crude.

Russian crude is increasingly filling the Middle East supply gap.

The short trade is starting to look overcrowded.

Nvidia is making history:

Nvidia, $NVDA, now accounts for ~8% of the S&P 500’s market cap, near its highest proportion on record.

The company's market value is now larger than that of 5 of the S&P 500's 11 sectors.

Only Information Technology, Communication Services, Financials, Health Care, Consumer Discretionary, and Industrials are larger.

Nvidia's market cap also exceeds the combined value of the Energy, Utilities, Real Estate, and Materials sectors.

At $5.3 trillion, Nvidia is now worth the equivalent of 16.3% of US GDP.

Nvidia’s rise has been historic.

Could US payrolls post another decline on Friday?

The number of hires fell by -278,000 in July, to 5.05 million, the lowest since February.

At the same time, total separations, the number of workers leaving their jobs through quits, layoffs or other departures, dropped -265,000, to 5.07 million, the lowest since April.

As a result, the difference between hires and separations widened to -18,000 in July, from -5,000 in June, its biggest gap since February.

This gap provides a rough indication of the direction of payroll growth and was broadly consistent with the official -23,000 payroll print in July.

Hires have now fallen below separations for 3 consecutive months, pointing to continued weakness in net job creation.

Because the hires and separations data feed into the payrolls calculation, the persistently negative gap suggests the official August payrolls figure could still have room to fall, raising the possibility of another negative print on Friday.

The US job market continues to appear weak.

The Bitcoin bull market is back.

It’s just not evenly distributed.

A strange dynamic swims beneath the surface of Bitcoin sentiment. Something you won’t pick up just by scrolling your timeline. The market mood has shifted, but many people refuse to believe it.

Negative price action and incessant infighting have led people to think good things are destined to fail in Bitcoin.

And this makes sense if you’ve only been in Bitcoin for a short period of time. Anyone who’s invested in the Orange Coin after 2021 likely feels disappointed by the price action. The euphoric gains and $1,000,000 price predictions haven't yet materialized.

But wouldn’t it be interesting if the people who’d been around longer were much more bullish than the rest?

“Sure, dude, but you can’t just measure something like that.”

You can.

I did.

It’s precisely this topic we’re going to dive DEEP into today. This group is deviating from the rest of Bitcoiners, and I believe it’s an incredibly bullish signal.

TLDR: OGs are beginning to show much more optimism, conviction, and activity than newer market participants.

BREAKING: The 30Y Treasury yield has traded above 5.00% for 56 trading days so far in 2026, the longest such streak in any year since 2006.

The 30Y Treasury yield has also stayed above this threshold for 41 consecutive trading sessions.

By comparison, 2023 saw only 7 such days, while 2007 recorded 50 days.

This comes as the 30Y Treasury yield has surged +47 basis points year-to-date to 5.28% and hit its highest level since 2007.

As a result, the 30Y Treasury yield has averaged 4.96% so far in 2026, on track for its highest annual level since 2004.

If the year ends at current levels, this would mark the 6th consecutive annual increase, with the yield more than triple its 2020 level of ~1.50%.

Higher for longer is here to stay.
